name: Sadza ne nyama
subtitle: Sadza ne nyama is sadza, a stiff dish of maize meal, eaten with nyama (meat) and a vegetable relish; it is described as the national dish of most Zimbabweans.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Sadza (maize meal) with nyama (meat) and a vegetable relish, described as the national dish of most Zimbabweans.

facts.label: Place in the diet
facts.value: White maize sadza is the most eaten food in Zimbabwe.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Sadza is considered almost a sacred food, and a meal is not a meal without it.

facts.label: Who cooks it
facts.value: By about ten years old most Shona children have learned to cook sadza.

facts.label: Relish
facts.value: One of the most common relishes with sadza and nyama is rape greens mixed with peanut butter.

facts.label: Meat
facts.value: Meat is often not on the menu, even in rural areas, because it is expensive to raise or buy.

facts.label: Other grains
facts.value: Sadza is also made from rapoko (finger millet), called sadza rezviyo.

facts.label: Where it is eaten
facts.value: Sadza, nyama and relish are eaten both at home and in restaurants.

facts.label: Change
facts.value: In the 2000s drought and food shortages threatened maize sadza, and small-grain porridge and sadza became more popular in rural and urban households.

parts.text: Sadza ne nyama is sadza, a stiff dish of maize meal, eaten with nyama (meat) and a vegetable relish; it is described as the national dish of most Zimbabweans. White maize sadza is the most eaten food in Zimbabwe, though sadza is also made from small grains such as rapoko (finger millet).

It is eaten at home and in restaurants, in towns and in the countryside; a common relish is rape greens mixed with peanut butter, and because meat is expensive many households often eat sadza with relish alone.
